# frostphp

> A deny-by-default capability linter for PHP. A one-screen policy in plain
> words says what the code may do; the check fails on anything else. Reads
> PHP 5 source on a PHP 8 runtime, separates capability from vulnerability,
> and separates include-time from call-time.

frostphp is the PHP sibling of frostpy (Python) and frostjs (JavaScript).
Install with `composer require --dev keithadler/frostphp`; the binary is
`vendor/bin/frostphp`.

## Commands

- `frostphp <paths>` - check against the nearest `frostphp.policy`. Exit 0
  clean, 1 on a finding, 2 on an error.
- `frostphp init <paths>` - write a policy granting what the code does today.
- `frostphp audit <paths>` - no policy: what does this code reach for?
- `frostphp deps [root]` - what runs at Composer install time, and what runs on
  every request via `autoload.files`.
- `frostphp summary` - the policy in plain English.
- `frostphp explain <capability>` - what it is and how to grant it.
- `frostphp capabilities` - the taxonomy.

Options: `--policy`, `--format text|json|sarif|github`, `--baseline`,
`--update-baseline`, `--diff <ref>`, `--php <version>`, `--ext <list>`,
`--include-vendor`, `--no-taint`, `--name`, `--today`.

## Policy grammar

```
policy "<name>"
extends "<path>"
may use <capability> [in "<glob>"] [until YYYY-MM-DD]
forbid <capability>
```

`--` starts a comment. Everything not granted is denied. A `forbid` beats a
`may use`, and an inherited `forbid` cannot be granted away by a child policy.
In globs, `*` and `?` stop at `/` and `**` crosses it.

## Capability families

codegen, process, network, filesystem, include, deserialize, scope, native,
env, response, database. A policy may name a family or one member
(`network.curl`). A family grant covers its members; a member grant does not
cover the family. Full list: docs/CAPABILITIES.md.

## The two questions, kept apart

- A capability is a fact about the code: `exec('ls')`. It belongs in the policy.
- A taint flow is a bug: `exec($_GET['c'])`. No policy line can grant it away.

## Distinctive to PHP

- `include $page` is a capability of its own family, because in PHP choosing
  code at runtime uses the same keyword as ordinary modularity.
- `extract($_GET)`, `$$name` and `parse_str($q)` rewrite the local scope from
  data.
- `phar://` makes any path function a deserializer, including `file_exists`.
- SQL findings are judged by where the value lands: escaped-and-quoted is safe,
  escaped-but-bare or in an `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` position is still injection.
- `addslashes` is not treated as a sanitiser.
- Escaping is per destination: escaped for SQL is not escaped for HTML.
- PHP 5 source is read on a PHP 8 runtime; short open tags are rewritten before
  parsing rather than silently parsed as HTML.
